title: AlgoExpert · All Kinds Of Node Depths

slides.heading: All Kinds Of Node Depths
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve All Kinds Of Node Depths, a very hard binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Sum, over every node, of the depths of all nodes in its subtree (relative to it).
Per subtree: sumDepths = sumDepths(l) + size(l) + sumDepths(r) + size(r).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Sum, over every node, of the depths of all nodes in its subtree (relative to it). Per subtree: sumDepths equals sumDepths(l) plus size(l) plus sumDepths(r) plus size(r).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each subtree's depth sum follows from its children's: their sums plus their sizes.
slides.narration: Each subtree's depth sum follows from its children's: their sums plus their sizes.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Compute depth sum for every subtree separately → O(n²)
Single post-order returning (size, depthSum, total) → O(n)
slides.narration: Computing each subtree's depth sum separately is quadratic. One post-order pass returning size, depth sum and total is linear.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Post-order returns size, depth sum and total
2. Depth sum equals children's sums plus their sizes
slides.narration: Step by step. First, post-order returns size, depth sum and total. Second, depth sum equals children's sums plus their sizes. Third, add everyone's depth sums.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Leaves: size 1, depth sum 0
slides.narration: Each node returns its subtree size, the sum of depths below it, and the running total.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: depths = left depths + left size + right depths + right size

slides.caption: Moving up adds 1 per node below
slides.narration: Moving up one level adds one to every node's depth below, so depth sum is children's sums plus their sizes.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: answer = Σ depth sums of all subtrees = 26

slides.caption: Answer: 26
slides.narration: Adding every subtree's depth sum gives 26.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Info returns zeros for null. Otherwise it combines children: size is one plus both, depths is each child's depth sum plus its size, and total adds the children's totals.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Each subtree's depth sum follows from its children's: their sums plus their sizes.
slides.narration: To recap All Kinds Of Node Depths: Each subtree's depth sum follows from its children's: their sums plus their sizes. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
